theme: 3 terms on app settings in Info.plist: the settings file, the name under the icon, and the build number

terms.definition: A settings file in your app that stores its name, version and other basic information.
terms.example: Open the Info.plist and check the app name.
terms.code:
let info = Bundle.main.infoDictionary
let name = info?["CFBundleName"] as? String

terms.definition: The app name shown under its icon on the Home Screen.
terms.example: The Display Name is too long, so iOS cuts it off.
terms.code:
let info = Bundle.main.infoDictionary
let shown = info?["CFBundleDisplayName"]

terms.definition: The build number of your app, which must go up with every App Store upload.
terms.example: Increase the Bundle Version, or App Store Connect will reject the build.

quizzes.question: What do you call the build number that must go up with every App Store upload?
What do you call the settings file that stores your app's name and version?
What do you call the app name shown under its icon on the Home Screen?

video.description:
Learn to explain what Info.plist holds for an iOS app: Info.plist, Display Name & Bundle Version, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Info.plist - A settings file in your app that stores its name, version and other basic information.
Display Name - The app name shown under its icon on the Home Screen.
Bundle Version - The build number of your app, which must go up with every App Store upload.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: iOS Info.plist, Display Name & Bundle Version | Day 119
landscape.description:
Explain Info.plist, Display Name & Bundle Version in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Info.plist, 디스플레이 이름, 번들 버전 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Info.plist - A settings file in your app that stores its name, version and other basic information.
한국어: Info.plist: 앱 이름, 버전 같은 기본 정보를 담은 설정 파일

Display Name - The app name shown under its icon on the Home Screen.
한국어: 디스플레이 이름: 홈 화면 아이콘 아래에 보이는 앱 이름

Bundle Version - The build number of your app, which must go up with every App Store upload.
한국어: 번들 버전: 앱스토어 업로드마다 올라가야 하는 앱의 빌드 번호

In this video, Mina and Jake fix a rejected upload and shorten the app name, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Info.plist, Display Name and Bundle Version in English?

dialogue.title: The rejected build

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, App Store Connect rejected my upload.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Bundle Version is not higher than the last build.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Raise the build number in the Info.plist.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is the Bundle Version the same as the app version?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. Users see the app version. The Bundle Version is the build number.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Understood. Also, the Display Name under the icon is too long.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then shorten it in the Info.plist.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I read the Display Name in code?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, from `infoDictionary`, like in the code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Remember, the Info.plist is the source of truth.

dialogue.code:
let info = Bundle.main.infoDictionary
let name = info?["CFBundleDisplayName"]
let build = info?["CFBundleVersion"]
